title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Zimbabwe, ICSP strengthened community and district‑level WASH systems in Matabeleland South, improving safe‑water access and resilience to water‑related health risks. Through borehole rehabilitation, repairs and new installations, 39,382 people gained reliable access to clean water, supported by trained water point committees who now manage operations and maintenance. Awareness efforts during cholera and Mpox outbreaks reached 54,355 people in Harare and 17,625 in Matabeleland South, helping communities adopt safer hygiene practices. Disaster preparedness collaboration with seven government partners further benefited 26,238 people, enhancing readiness for WASH‑related emergencies and improving local capacity to prevent disease.. Together with the Government of Zimbabwe's Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA), the programme aims to increase household access to water, sanitation and hygiene services. Interventions are aimed at repairing and rehabilitating boreholes and establishing piped water schemes, as well as establishing community-led Waterpoint Management Committees (WMCs) to manage the water points. Social Behaviour Change (SBC) interventions aim to providing individuals, families and communities the knowledge, skills and self-efficacy they need to adopt positive WASH household practices.
